clue.text: Times, reprinted badly, read wrongly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters before it come out in a muddled order

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter as the material

explanation.surface: A newspaper story reprinted with errors has been misunderstood by its readers.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinterpret something is to understand or construe it incorrectly, so the past participle matches 'read wrongly'.

clue.text: Doctor harming records, resulting in dismissal

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters that follow are falsified into a new order

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter as the material

explanation.surface: A physician who damages patient files is fired for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person being sacked, but it is the verb telling you to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given your marching orders is an idiom for being sent away or sacked from a job.

clue.text: Third part in examination might be least hard

parts.note: the third letter of the four-letter word for an examination
a part 'in' something is a part of it
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: The third section of an exam might turn out to be the easiest one.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay describes itself: S is the third letter 'of TEST', and the answer is written out as S + OF + TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft is an antonym of hard, so the superlative softest means the least hard.

clue.text: Old person that is somehow different than an elder

indicators.note: made different in some way, so the letters are rearranged into another order

parts.note: all three words taken letter for letter as the material

explanation.surface: An elderly person who seems oddly unlike a respected village elder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old person' is a joke definition: a Neanderthal was an early human from the Stone Age.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neanderthal is a prehistoric human species, so literally a person from very old times; also slang for an old-fashioned type.

clue.text: Nominally important role, so to speak, in modern establishment

definitions.text: Nominally important role, so to speak

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone holds a prestigious-sounding job title in a modern firm.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oscar Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest, being called Ernest is what makes a man important, so the role is important by name; 'so to speak' nods to the earnest/Ernest pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is the name both lead suitors claim in Wilde's comedy, where the name itself carries the importance.

clue.text: Arranged probe into earnings for youth providing daily service

indicators.note: arranged means put into a fresh order, so the next word's letters are reordered
one piece goes into the other, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: pay is what you earn
the word's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An organised inquiry into the wages of a young worker who does a daily round.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperboy is a boy who delivers newspapers every day, hence a youth giving a daily service.

clue.text: Outgoing movement featured in web blog

indicators.note: something featured in a text appears within it, so look inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A trend leaving the internet is reported in an online blog.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb is the outward flow of the tide as it goes back out to sea.

clue.text: English scholar including it with current version

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a don is a university teacher
taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An English academic, plus something up to date, makes the current version of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher, the crossword's usual scholar; I is the physics symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one particular printed form or version of a book or other publication.

clue.text: University position — risks pinning list up with it

indicators.note: to pin something is to hold it fast, here gripped inside another word

parts.note: to chance something is to risk it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a roll is a list of names
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A university post holder gambles by posting a list upside down, trying to look trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' is slang for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities have a chancellor as titular head, and chancellorship is the office or position held.

clue.text: Desist from much-repeated saying

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to hold back from doing something
second meaning: a noun, a phrase or chorus said over and over

explanation.surface: Stop using a tired catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb takes 'from' just as desist does, so 'Desist from' swaps whole for 'refrain from'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means abstain; as a noun it is a recurring chorus or oft-heard remark.

clue.text: Put out book with line I added in press

indicators.note: added in means slotted inside, so the earlier pieces go within the next word

parts.note: to press is to push
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A book is issued with an extra line written in for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers but is the verb meaning push.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a book or magazine is to issue it to the public, which is to publish it.

clue.text: Work in garden, with no tree or bush to prune, finally

definitions.text: Work in garden, with no tree or bush to prune

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of each word in the stretch named

parts.note: the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Gardening work when there are no shrubs or trees needing to be cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the job, while the last letters of 'with no tree' spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoe is to weed and loosen soil with a long-handled tool, garden work that involves no pruning.

clue.text: For amusement, take back painting etc, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: one piece placed in the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: diction is one's way of speaking

indicators.note: taking something back returns it the way it came, so its letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: painting and the like are the arts

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws a painting for fun, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' reads as a phrase meaning 'so to speak', but 'in' is the insertion signal and the rest is DICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A distraction is a diversion or entertainment that takes the mind off other things.

clue.text: Something said about piece or section

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a comment is a remark
a part is a piece

explanation.surface: A remark made concerning a particular passage or section of text.
explanation.definitionFit: A compartment is a separate section of a container, train carriage or the like.

clue.text: Type scientific publication

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the long-running British science journal

explanation.surface: A kind of research journal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature means kind or sort, and Nature is also the title of a famous weekly science journal.

clue.text: Amount divided by people about to start

indicators.note: a word divided by others is split open with them in the middle

parts.note: as in 'the bill comes to', to amount to
men are people
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A sum of money is shared among a group who are on the point of beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amount' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in what a total comes to.
explanation.definitionFit: To commence is a formal word for to begin or start.

clue.text: Driver, for example, that's needed here

definitions.text: Driver, for example, that's needed here

parts.note: surface reading: a motorist, and the place where one is wanted
setter's reading: the long-hitting golf stick, and also the venue where it is used, so the answer names both the tool and the place

explanation.walkthrough: The answer means both a stick for hitting the ball and the course premises where you play, so the driver is one and is needed at the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is a type of golf club, and a golf club is also the members' venue where it is used.

clue.text: Sound of nocturnal hunter, initially from small branch

parts.note: as in getting off a bus, away from it
standard abbreviation
the call of an owl

explanation.surface: An owl's cry comes first from a little branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' says the last two pieces go before the owl's call.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a side shoot growing from a plant's main stem, so a branch.

clue.text: Bat, making fine half-century, say

parts.note: pencil grading abbreviation for fine
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, half of a hundred
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman scores a lovely fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, where 'bat' and 'half-century' (fifty runs) belong, but bat is the verb used of eyelashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To bat your eyelashes is to flutter them, so the verbs share this sense.

clue.text: Names of two men hunting animal in Africa

parts.note: the first man's name
the second man's name

explanation.surface: Two men, named, are out hunting a beast on safari.
explanation.walkthrough: The fragment supplies two common male names, Jack and Al, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackal is a wild dog of Africa and Asia that hunts and scavenges.

clue.text: Man checked, holding one place for author

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it within, so the outer word surrounds the rest

parts.note: in chess the king is the man that is put in check
Roman numeral one
abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A man is detained in a particular spot by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' in chess is any piece; the one that is checked is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling was the English author of The Jungle Book and Just So Stories.

clue.text: Couple of females breaking up fight or rough stuff

indicators.note: breaking up a word splits it open so the other piece sits in the gap

parts.note: a duel is a fight between two
F twice, the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Two women intervene to stop a brawl or some violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough stuff' sounds like violence but means a coarse cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Duffel is a coarse, heavy woollen fabric, used for duffel coats and bags.

clue.text: Repeated failure in court, conceding point

definitions.meaning: first meaning: two failed serves in a row on a tennis court
second meaning: the tennis error that hands a point to the opponent

explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a double fault is two faulty serves in succession, which loses the server the point.

clue.text: 'Old Man River' as standard

parts.note: 'old man' is slang for father, pa
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The song Ol' Man River treated as a jazz standard.
explanation.walkthrough: Ol' Man River is the famous song from Show Boat, a standard in the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or expected level, the standard against which things are measured.

clue.text: Like part of eye stored in secret in a lab

indicators.note: something stored in a place is kept inside it, so look within the following words

parts.note: runs across four words of the phrase

explanation.surface: An eye specimen is kept secretly in a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinal is the adjective for the retina, the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.

clue.text: Sign agreement Mafia boss set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised from the bottom, so the word reads upward

parts.note: a Mafia chief is called a don

explanation.surface: A mob leader is framed into signing a pact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign agreement' looks like 'sign a contract' but is a verb phrase meaning show assent.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod is to signal yes with a dip of the head, a gesture of assent.

clue.text: Misrepresented himself in European language

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown falsely, so the letters are presented in a wrong order

parts.note: taken letter for letter as the material

explanation.surface: A man gave a false account of himself in a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Flemish is the Dutch dialect spoken in Flanders, northern Belgium.

clue.text: Clubs chat about what diners require — good reason not to buy something

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the following pieces

parts.note: card-suit abbreviation
to rap is to talk freely
diners need their food to be fit to eat
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Golf clubs' gossip about restaurant needs offers good grounds for not purchasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good' seems to belong to the definition 'good reason not to buy something', but it is wordplay, leaving 'reason not to buy something' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A credibility gap is a gulf between claims and reality, which makes people disbelieve, and so not buy, what is offered.
